prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, haloperidol or other centrally acting D2-blocking antiemetics or antipsychotics; if an antipsychotic is needed, use quetiapine or clozapine
Do not prescribe centrally acting anticholinergics (trihexyphenidyl, benztropine) in older adults or in any patient with cognitive impairment
required_recommendations: Diagnose clinically probable PD (MDS 2015): bradykinesia with right-hand rest tremor and rigidity, no absolute exclusion, no red flag; the response to levodopa may add a supportive criterion [Postuma_2015]

Start carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg, half a tablet three times daily with food, increasing over 2 to 4 weeks to one tablet three times daily (300 mg/day levodopa), and review the response after 2 to 3 months, titrating to the clinical response because absorption may be less predictable after gastric bypass, and measuring lying and standing blood pressure at each step on metoprolol [NICE_NG71]
If a dopamine agonist is used, warn about impulse control disorders and excessive daytime sleepiness and ask about them at every visit [NICE_NG71]
Treat the depression actively: review the fluoxetine dose and response and offer psychological therapy; if an MAO-B inhibitor is considered later, avoid combining it with fluoxetine
Refer for physiotherapy for posture (Pisa syndrome), gait and balance, with a regular exercise programme

key_clinical_evidence: Right-predominant bradykinesia with decrement, cogwheel rigidity and a 4-5 Hz pill-rolling rest tremor of the right hand that spread to the left hand after a year: parkinsonism with one supportive criterion (rest tremor) [Postuma_2015]
No red flag: no falls in 20 months, an orthostatic fall of 12/6 mmHg, urgency without incontinence, asymmetric signs; no levodopa trial yet, so clinically probable PD [Postuma_2015]
MRI with Fazekas 1 foci only and normal midbrain, pons and putamina: no vascular, NPH or atypical-parkinsonism signature

Stooped posture and depressed mood are common in PD; Pisa posture also occurs in PD, and although early postural deformity is a supportive MSA feature, MSA criteria are not met without urge incontinence, orthostatic hypotension or cerebellar signs
Gastric bypass 7 years ago without signs of myelopathy or neuropathy (normal vibration, proprioception and reflexes, flexor plantars): no clinical picture of copper or B12 deficiency

interactions: Fluoxetine with an MAO-B inhibitor: serotonin syndrome is rare, but fluoxetine and fluvoxamine are best avoided with rasagiline; at least 5 weeks should pass between stopping fluoxetine and starting rasagiline.

Metoprolol lowers standing blood pressure and adds to the orthostatic fall; levodopa can lower it further. Review the need for each and measure lying and standing blood pressure at each levodopa dose step.
Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6 and raises metoprolol concentrations: watch the heart rate.
warnings: Levodopa is absorbed in the proximal small intestine: after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass its absorption may be less predictable, so titrate to the clinical response.
Metformin, insulin glargine and levothyroxine: no clinically relevant interaction with levodopa; separate levothyroxine from other morning medicines as usual.
High-protein meals can reduce levodopa absorption; distribute protein evenly through the day.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. Delgado is a 69-year-old right-handed woman referred to the Movement Disorders Clinic by her primary care physician for evaluation of progressive motor symptoms over the past 20 months. She first noticed a tremor in her right hand approximately 20 months ago, together with a general sense of slowness. The tremor is most noticeable at rest, such as when her hand is resting on her lap while watching television, and partially improves with intentional movements like reaching for objects. Over the past 8 months, a milder tremor has appeared intermittently in the left hand. She has not fallen; she nearly fell once while turning quickly in her kitchen and steadied herself on the counter. Her daughter has noticed that her mother's posture has become increasingly stooped and that she appears to lean to one side when sitting or standing. The patient reports progressive difficulty with handwriting, noting that her letters have become smaller and harder to read. Buttoning shirts and opening jars have become increasingly effortful. She has experienced worsening insomnia, with frequent nighttime awakenings and difficulty returning to sleep. She endorses a depressed mood over the past several months, with decreased interest in her usual activities including gardening and reading. She reports urinary urgency and increased frequency without incontinence. She occasionally feels briefly lightheaded when she stands up quickly in the morning, without near-syncope or loss of consciousness. She denies visual hallucinations, acting out dreams, or any symptoms suggestive of REM sleep behavior disorder. She denies obsessive-compulsive behaviors. Her appetite has been stable and weight has been steady.

neurological_exam.additional: Resting tremor of the right hand at approximately 4-5 Hz, pill-rolling, re-emergent with sustained posture; milder intermittent rest tremor of the left hand. Orthostatic vital signs: supine BP 148/88 with HR 68, standing BP 136/82 with HR 76 after 3 minutes (12 mmHg systolic and 6 mmHg diastolic fall). No carotid bruits.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing intact bilaterally without dysmetria. No dysdiadochokinesia beyond that attributable to bradykinesia. Heel-to-shin testing mildly slow but accurate.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full without nystagmus. No vertical gaze palsy. Facial expression mildly hypomimic bilaterally. Tongue midline without fasciculations. Palate elevates symmetrically.
neurological_exam.gait: Narrow-based gait with reduced arm swing, right more than left. Short, shuffling steps. Difficulty initiating turns, which take 4 steps. Stooped posture. Pull test: two steps of retropulsion, recovers unaided. No festination or freezing.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented to person, place, time, and situation. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score 26/30, losing one point on cube copy, two on delayed recall (3/5 words) and one on verbal fluency. Attention and language preserved. Affect mildly depressed.
neurological_exam.motor: Bradykinesia with decrement on finger tapping, hand movements and toe tapping, right more than left. Moderate cogwheel rigidity at the right wrist and elbow, mild rigidity at the left wrist. No pyramidal weakness. Tone mildly increased in the lower extremities, right more than left. Stooped posture. Pisa syndrome noted with trunk leaning to the left.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, patellar 2+ bilaterally, ankle 1+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffman sign.
